reading.body:
H.R. 7110 is a one-party bill: Summer Lee sponsors it and all sixteen cosponsors are Democrats.

The support is broad within that party but not deep. Seventeen members signed on, drawn from across the Democratic caucus, and no Republican is recorded among them. A bill with that shape can move through a House under Democratic control and has little path in a chamber where it does not. The bill's own text tags it to bias and civil rights, which places it in the algorithmic-accountability family rather than in the compute, data center, or grid policy that governs how much AI capacity gets built.

The lobbying record is the notable absence. No filing from 2025 or later names this bill, which means the organizations that usually weigh in on AI regulation have not registered it as an issue in their disclosures. That is a statement about attention, not about support or opposition. A filing that names a bill shows only that the bill came up, never which side the filer took.

What this does not cover: the bill's provisions, its committee status, any vote, and any position taken by industry. The data records sponsorship, cosponsorship, and the absence of named lobbying activity as of the latest status date of 2026-01-15. It says nothing about whether the bill advances, and nothing about how its rules would interact with the power and building constraints that limit AI scaling.
